rationale: The pain is real and acute — 432 CVEs in 24 hours is a concrete, documented stress event, and security teams at Linux-infrastructure companies already spend real budget on Snyk, Wiz, and Qualys, confirming willingness to pay. The buyer is identifiable (security engineers and SREs at mid-to-large companies running Linux at scale), but the build_gates are the decisive blocker: buildability and operational autonomy both fall short, because accurate CVE-to-kernel-version relevance mapping requires ingesting live kernel metadata, distro patch feeds, and customer environment data — well beyond a Claude prompt and a Stripe link. Delivery would require per-customer environment setup and ongoing data pipeline maintenance, making this a systems-integration product rather than an autonomous AI micro-service for a solo non-technical operator.
solution_plan: The micro-service would be a kernel CVE relevance filter: customers submit their kernel version and distro, and Claude cross-references incoming CVE feeds to flag only those that actually apply. Building it would require: ingesting NVD/CVE feeds automatically, mapping CVEs to kernel version ranges and distro patch status (data that changes daily and requires reliable parsing of structured kernel security advisories), and presenting a filtered dashboard or digest — this goes well beyond a simple prompt+page+Stripe stack and needs real data-pipeline and integration engineering. Selling would target security engineers via LinkedIn outreach or communities like r/netsec and the CISA/NVD mailing lists, but those channels require technical credibility and a working demo before any serious buyer engages. Maintaining it means keeping the CVE ingestion pipeline current, handling edge cases in kernel version matching, and supporting customer-specific configurations — all of which require ongoing technical judgment, not just Claude approvals. As a solo non-technical operator, the build and maintenance burden here is beyond the factory's autonomous capability in its current form; this would need a technical co-founder or a contracted engineer to build the data infrastructure before it could run hands-off.
notes: Fails build_gates: operational_autonomy (4, minimum 7) and buildability_with_ai (4, minimum 6). The core challenge is that CVE-to-kernel-version relevance is a structured data-matching problem requiring live feed ingestion and version-range logic — not a natural-language task Claude can handle reliably with prompt engineering alone. Recommend validating buyer interest and willingness to pay first (a simple waitlist page + outreach to security teams) before investing in any build.
